title: MiniMax-Music3: Full Songs From Lyrics Plus a Description
hook: A five-minute song with coherent structure and expressive vocals, from an 8B model that plans the arrangement and a 0.6B model that fills in the audio frame by frame.
key_points: Generates complete songs up to five minutes long from lyrics plus a structured music description.
Hybrid design: an 8B global LLM handles long-range musical structure, a 0.6B local LLM handles frame-level acoustic detail.
Synthesis uses Flow Matching and a Flow-VAE over continuous hidden states, with eight-layer residual vector quantization (RVQ) tokenization.
Outputs 32 kHz, 16-bit stereo WAV; prompts are capped at 5,000 tokens.
Lyrics accept section tags like [Verse] and [Chorus]; descriptions control genre, instrumentation, vocal performance, and arrangement.
Runs via SGLang-Omni, Diffusers, and ComfyUI, requires CUDA, and is published under a Creative Commons license.
content_html: MiniMax released Music3, a music generation model that takes lyrics plus a structured description and returns a complete song — up to five minutes of 32 kHz stereo audio with expressive vocals and a coherent arrangement.
extra_html:
The architecture is the interesting part, and it's a clean example of splitting a problem by time scale. An 8B global LLM handles long-range structure — where the chorus goes, how the arrangement develops — while a 0.6B local LLM handles frame-level acoustic detail. Waveform synthesis runs through Flow Matching and a Flow-VAE over continuous hidden states, with eight-layer residual vector quantization for tokenization. Control comes from two channels: lyrics that accept section tags like [Verse] and [Chorus], and a separate description covering genre, instrumentation, vocal performance, and arrangement.

Practically: prompts cap at 5,000 tokens, inference needs CUDA, and it plugs into SGLang-Omni, Diffusers, and ComfyUI. The model card lists a Creative Commons license — worth reading the specific variant before commercial use, since CC terms vary considerably in what they permit.

related.title: MusicGen: Simple and Controllable Music Generation
related.hook: Generate music from a text description or a melody reference using a single autoregressive transformer over discrete audio tokens - no cascade of specialized models required.

related.title: Audex: A Unified Audio-Text LLM That Doesn't Forget How to Think
related.hook: Bolting audio onto a strong text model usually costs some of its reasoning. NVIDIA's Audex treats speech and text as one token stream, reporting top audio skills with little to no loss on text.

flashcards.prompt: Why does MiniMax-Music3 split work between an 8B and a 0.6B model?

choices.text: The 8B handles long-range musical structure while the 0.6B handles frame-level acoustic detail
The 0.6B is a draft model for speculative decoding of the 8B's output
The 8B generates vocals and the 0.6B generates instrumentation

flashcards.explanation_html: It's a division by time scale, not by instrument or by speed: song-level coherence needs capacity, per-frame acoustics need throughput.
